last_transition_reason: The argument correctly fixes n and an arbitrary t in [0,1), defines a=floor(nt), and proves E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n) by termwise monotonicity of floor under multiplication by positive k, followed by summation. The conclusion matches the lemma exactly and no forbidden dependencies are used.
latest_nl_proof:
Let n>1 be fixed, let t be real with 0<=t<1, and set a=floor(n t). Then by definition of the floor function,
a <= n t < a+1,
so dividing by n gives
a/n <= t < (a+1)/n.
In particular, t >= a/n.

Now for each k=1,...,n, since k>0 we have k t >= k(a/n), and the floor function is monotone increasing, hence
floor(k t) >= floor(k a/n).
Dividing by the positive integer k preserves the inequality:
floor(k t)/k >= floor(k a/n)/k.
Summing over k=1,...,n yields
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k >= sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a/n)/k.

Also, because a/n is a real number with n(a/n)=a, we have
floor(n(a/n)) = a = floor(n t).
Therefore
E_n(t) = floor(n t) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k
<= a - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a/n)/k
= E_n(a/n).
This is exactly the desired inequality.
role_in_parent: Compare the value at an arbitrary fractional input with the left endpoint of its 1/n-interval.
statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with 0 <= t < 1, if a = floor(n*t), then E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).

domain_restrictions: t is real and satisfies 0 <= t and t < 1
a equals floor(n*t) so a is an integer
since t < 1, n*t < n, hence a <= n-1
therefore a divided by n lies in the interval [0, 1)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1 and all real numbers t with 0 <= t < 1, let a be floor(n*t). Then E_n(t) is less than or equal to E_n(a divided by n).
